incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired -> PD#INC-20260315-az2-high-latency (auto-trigger from region-health). brief: sustained tail latency > 2s for token-gen paths in az2
pagerduty: PagerDuty: Alert routed to team 'infra-sre' and #incidents. Escalation policy: immediate -> oncall -> team lead if not acked in 2m
Alex (oncall): ack'd via PD, jumping in. seeing initial spikes in p50->p99 for hosted generation. tagging @Maya and @Pradeep.
Maya (sre): I'm on it. can you confirm whether KV cache evictions spiked? grabbing metrics.
Pradeep (infra): NIC counters on 3 machines in az2 show RX errors + interface resets around 09:12UTC. could be a partial fabric NIC issue.
Samir (platform): routing telemetry shows increased request timeouts to model shard pool az2-pool-B. fallback routing already started for a small % by the smart-router 09:14UTC.
Alex (oncall): Customer-facing: hosted API p99 2.8s for region eu-2 (served from az2). We should activate spillover to eu-1 and us-west-az4 for latency-sensitive routes.
Maya (sre): Agreed. I'll open the routing override.
Samir (platform): running override command now:
```
# enable spill policy - route 30% of stateful to eu-1, 20% to us-west-az4
redwood-routing apply --region az2 --policy spill --weights eu-1=30,us-west-az4=20 --reason "az2 latency spike"
```
Samir (platform): override applied, router metrics show gradual diversion starting 09:18UTC. expect latency improvement within 1-2 minutes for new requests.
Alex (oncall): Noted. Can someone confirm autoscaler behavior? we don't want to scale into bad NICs.
Pradeep (infra): autoscaler set to not schedule new pods to nodes with NIC reset flag. I'll mark the 3 nodes as unschedulable and start evacuation.
Pradeep (infra): commands:
```
kubectl cordon node-az2-03
kubectl drain node-az2-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# repeat for node-az2-07, node-az2-09
```
Maya (sre): Confirmed. Evacuation in progress. KV cache rehydrate traffic spike expected; watch read latency. enabling KV cache prefetch throttling.
Alex (oncall): Support Ops - please prep an update for the status page: impact: increased API latency for hosted customers in eu-2; mitigation: traffic diversion to eu-1/us-west-az4; ETA next update in 15m.
Support Ops: Got it. Drafting message. Will post once we have diversion metrics.
Pradeep (infra): NIC vendor alerted. they're pulling firmware logs. early hypothesis: driver flake after recent firmware push to that rack.
Samir (platform): Router health: steady state: 22% of traffic now routed off az2. p99 latency down 18% for diverted traffic, overall p99 improved ~0.7s.
Maya (sre): We're seeing some 503s from one model shard that lost connection during eviction. Failover path is retrying to replica in eu-1, so errors are transient. Adding 5s retry window to client-side policy for affected endpoints.
Alex (oncall): Good. What's customer impact classification?
Maya (sre): Impact: degraded performance for eu-2 hosted customers, intermittent failed requests for a small subset (<=0.5% of requests) while replicas failover. Recommend "partial outage" on internal triage.
Samir (platform): Patch applied to router: reduce prefetched KV concurrency to avoid cascade rehydration.
Pradeep (infra): Vendor confirmed firmware regression on NIC batch; rolling back firmware on affected rack. Rolling back now; ETA ~12m for completion on 3 nodes.
Alex (oncall): If rollback finishes and nodes pass health checks, we'll gradually reintroduce capacity. Keep routing weight pinned until green.
Maya (sre): Agree. I'll monitor model-serving p99 and KV cache hit rate.
incident-bot: PD update -> INC-20260315: Acknowledged by Alex at 09:16UTC. Next escalation in 10m if unacknowledged.
pagerduty: Notification: PagerDuty escalation suppressed (ack received).
Support Ops: Status page draft: "We are investigating elevated latency in EU region. Traffic is being diverted; some customers may experience degraded performance. Engineers are actively mitigating. Updates every 15 minutes." Posting now.
Support Ops: status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20260315 posted :package:
Alex (oncall): Handing off to @Maya for follow-up and postmortem ownership. I'm stepping off after stabilization.
Maya (sre): Taking incident lead. I'll coordinate postmortem and RCA. tagging @Pradeep for infra action items and @Samir for routing follow-ups.
Pradeep (infra): rollback completed on nodes; NIC counters stable. Starting health probes and reallow scheduling.
Samir (platform): routing weights: scaling back diversion to 10% -> 0% over next 10m as nodes come healthy.
Maya (sre): p99 back to baseline ~09:46UTC for most routes. transient errors resolved.
incident-bot: Incident update: INC-20260315 -> status changed to 'mitigated' at 09:48UTC.
Support Ops: Updating status page to 'mitigated' and adding note about ongoing RCA.
Maya (sre): Postmortem owners: Maya (lead), Pradeep (infra), Samir (routing). Action items: 1) Add NIC regression detection to canary checks, 2) refine router spill thresholds to be faster, 3) improve cache rehydrate throttling default.
Alex (oncall): Thanks team. I'll add a short handoff note in oncall. :thumbsup:
Samir (platform): one more follow-up: adding a short-term rule to prevent autoscaler from placing new pods on recently-firmware-changed nodes for 24h.
Maya (sre): Noted. I'll schedule RCA meeting and draft mitigation timeline.
StatusBot: Reminder created: INC-20260315 postmortem meeting scheduled for 2026-03-16 15:00UTC.
Pradeep (infra): closing my tasks as nodes stabilized. will attach firmware logs to the postmortem ticket.
Maya (sre): Closing thread. Thanks all.
